hint.text: The white areas on the map show polar deserts, and the yellow areas show hot deserts.

atoms.text: Deserts are areas with very low rainfall. There are two types, hot deserts and polar deserts.
Hot deserts are extremely hot, with daytime summer temperatures often exceeding 40 °C. These scorching conditions mean that only specialised animals and plants can survive.

Polar deserts experience extremely cold temperatures and barely any rainfall because the air is too cold to hold any moisture. There are also very few plants and animals that are able to survive there.

atoms.a: What are the two types of desert called?
What is the climate like in polar deserts?

instruction.text: Drag the Sahara onto the North of Africa to find out more.

feedback.end: The Sahara Desert is the largest hot desert in the world, stretching across nearly the whole of North Africa.

atoms.b: Around 25% of the Sahara ((Ocean ++Desert)) is covered in sand dunes.
Sand dunes are formed when grains of ((water ++sand)) are blown by the wind to form a mound or ridge.
They are mostly found in deserts but can also be found on ((buildings ++beaches)).

instruction.text: The living things in deserts have adapted to their environment. Select the image that matches the description.

atoms.a: These plants have long roots that collect water from a large area. Their thick stems also allow them to store water.
These animals have scaly, camouflaged skin, which helps them to blend in with the desert. Their claws help them to run across the sand.
These animals store fat in their humps, which lets them go long periods without water. They also have long eyelashes to protect against sand.
